title: Cost Surgeon: staged batching & KV-cache recommendation cards, drift-aware diff preview and immutable apply ledger
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Teams running inference at scale need a clear, low-risk way to accept automated batching/caching recommendations that materially reduce per-token costs without degrading tail latency or correctness. Current Optimize flows show suggestions but lack a deterministic preview, runtime drift detection, and an auditable immutable ledger for applied config changes.

Proposal: Ship a unified UX called 'Cost Surgeon' — a set of recommendation cards that present one-click staged changes (batching/window sizes, KV cache TTLs/prefix policies, quantization knobs), a drift-aware diff preview that compares proposed config to the live runtime and highlights potential semantic differences, and an immutable apply ledger that records pre/post runtime snapshots, operator, justification, and automatic rollback hooks. The flow should support sandboxed dry-runs, canary rollout policies, and a machine-readable audit trail for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards surface batching + KV-cache suggestions with estimated cost delta (tokens/$. month) and expected p50/p95 latency impact.
Diff preview overlays: show exact key/value changes, highlight runtime drift (config drift since suggestion generated), and flag incompatible runtime constraints (e.g., reserved capacity limits).
Staged apply flow: users can stage multiple suggestions, run a sandbox dry-run returning simulated metrics, then commit a timestamped apply that records before/after snapshots.

Immutable apply ledger: every committed apply produces an auditable entry with operator, PR/issue link, versioned config blob, and cryptographic hash (or opaque ledger id). Entries are immutable and support a one-click rollback that schedules a safe canary revert.
Console UX: card-level expand/collapse, compact summary rows, inline visual diff, and activity timeline item showing dry-run and live verification results.
Telemetry: events emitted for preview-open, dry-run-start/finish, apply-commit, rollback-initiate; dashboards updated to show cost saved and rollback rate.
Security: apply actions require role with 'optimize.apply' permission; ledger entries exportable as CSV/JSON for compliance audits.
tasks: PM: finalize card metadata fields and UX copy (cost estimate, confidence, risk).
Design: high-fidelity mocks for collapsed/expanded card, diff overlay, and ledger timeline (link to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/cost-surgeon).
Eng (Frontend): implement card component, diff overlay, staging UX, and interactions with ledger API.
Eng (Backend): ledger persistence model (append-only), dry-run simulator endpoint, drift detection job to compare live config snapshots, RBAC checks.
Eng (Runtime): expose necessary runtime snapshot endpoints: current batching config, kv-cache evictions/TTL, active quantization profile.
SRE/Infra: ensure sandbox dry-run runs against a synthetic traffic driver and cannot impact production capacity, add quotas to prevent abuse.
QA: test matrix for correctness, latency regressions (p50/p95), and rollback recovery in a dedicated staging cluster.
Docs: console help content, audit export format, and runbook for rollbacks (link to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Cost+Surgeon+Runbook).
notes_and_progress: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with design + runtime teams; alignment on primary metrics (cost delta, p95 latency, rollback success rate).
2026-03-04: Design spike produced two variants for diff UX: inline semantic diff vs side-by-side JSON diff. PM prefers semantic-first with JSON toggle.
2026-03-06: Runtime team flagged that KV-cache TTL changes require coordinated cache flush in some deployments — added a warning and an optional 'graceful warm-up' step.
2026-03-08: Security requested ledger export shape and retention profile; proposed retention 365 days and exportable JSON/CSV with ledger id hashes.

2026-03-09: Interim implementation plan: 2-week sprint for card UI + diff preview, parallel backend sprint for ledger API and dry-run simulator. GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10456.
Design feedback: prefer contextual help microcopy for recommendations to explain cost model assumptions and confidence buckets (High/Medium/Low).
Blocked items: need runtime API to return 'sequence-length distribution' for accurate cost estimates; dependency on ENG-221432 (runtime-metrics-export).
decisions: Keep recommendation cards actionable but reversible: no automatic auto-apply; all applies must go through staged commit with operator confirmation.
Use semantic diff highlighting by default (human-friendly), with ability to view raw JSON for auditors.
Ledger entries will be append-only and surfaced in Console but deletable only via retention policy by SRE (no per-entry deletion by users).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: a bad batching suggestion could increase tail latency. Mitigation: require synthetic dry-run and post-apply live verification step with automatic rollback if p95 worsens beyond threshold.
Risk: configuration drift between when suggestion was computed and when applied. Mitigation: show drift badge in preview and require user acknowledgement if drift > threshold.
Risk: compliance teams need immutable evidence. Mitigation: ledger exports with cryptographic hashes and operator metadata; integrate with existing audit logs.
stakeholders: Owners: Aisha Malik (PM), Diego Ramos (PM lead).
